title: 〜の極み
simpleExplanation: 〜の極み means "the very limit of X": 贅沢の極み (the height of luxury), 疲労の極み (utter exhaustion), 痛恨の極み (the bitterest regret). It is a noun phrase, so it can be the predicate (〜の極みだ) or take particles (疲労の極みに達する). It works for states of things and people, not just the speaker's own feelings.
whenUsed: Formal written Japanese: commentary, editorials, formal apologies (痛恨の極み is common in public statements). It can describe the speaker (感激の極み), a third party (疲労の極みにある選手) or a thing (贅沢の極み).
formation: N + の極み (贅沢・疲労・痛恨・感激・不幸・美)
〜の極みだ / 〜の極みに達する / 〜の極みにある

diagram.translation: With overtime day after day, the employees have reached the limit of exhaustion.

examples.ja: こんな豪華な料理を毎日食べるなんて、贅沢の極みだ。
examples.reading: こんなごうかなりょうりをまいにちたべるなんて、ぜいたくのきわみだ。
examples.en: Eating such lavish food every day is the height of luxury.
examples.note: 贅沢の極み is the most common phrase: luxury at its most extreme.

examples.ja: 連日の残業で、社員は疲労の極みに達している。
examples.reading: れんじつのざんぎょうで、しゃいんはひろうのきわみにたっしている。
examples.en: With overtime day after day, the employees have reached the limit of exhaustion.
examples.note: 疲労の極みに達する: a physical state of a third party, which の至り cannot describe.

examples.ja: あの一球を打てなかったのは痛恨の極みだ。
examples.reading: あのいっきゅうをうてなかったのはつうこんのきわみだ。
examples.en: Not hitting that one pitch is the bitterest regret.
examples.note: 痛恨の極み: used in public apologies and sports commentary.

examples.ja: 今回の不祥事は、当社にとって痛恨の極みであります。
examples.reading: こんかいのふしょうじは、とうしゃにとってつうこんのきわみであります。
examples.en: This scandal is a matter of the deepest regret for our company.
examples.note: Corporate apology style; であります is very formal.

examples.ja: あの職人の技は、まさに美の極みと言える。
examples.reading: あのしょくにんのわざは、まさにびのきわみといえる。
examples.en: That craftsman's skill can truly be called the pinnacle of beauty.
examples.note: の極み can describe a quality of a thing.

similarGrammar.difference: Limited to the speaker's own feeling in humble speech (光栄の至り). の極み is broader.
Same kanji, but attaches to na-adjectives to mean "extremely" (危険極まりない).
"As much as one can" (力の限り); a limit of effort, not the extreme of a state.

commonMistakes.wrong: 光栄の極みです。（受賞スピーチで）
commonMistakes.why: 光栄 is conventionally paired with の至り in speeches. Use の極み for 贅沢・疲労・痛恨.
The nouns are Sino-Japanese (漢語): 疲労, not 疲れ.

commonMistakes.wrong: この料理は贅沢極みだ。
commonMistakes.right: この料理は贅沢の極みだ。

usageNotes: The most frequent nouns: 贅沢・疲労・痛恨・感激・不幸・悲嘆・美・愚か.
痛恨の極み is a formula in apologies and post-match interviews; 贅沢の極み is often used half-jokingly.
の極みに達する / の極みにある are set verbal frames.
jlptTips: If the noun is 贅沢・疲労・痛恨, の極み is almost certainly the answer.
Distractors: の至り, 極まりない, の限り. Check the noun and whether a third party or a thing is described.
In 並べ替え, keep N + の極み together and look for だ / に達する after it.
